#### 1. Houge-Janssens syndrome 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.445)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9860927, Reactome:R-HSA-180024)

**Proposed mechanism:** PPP2R1A (HGNC:9000) —BINDS→ Protein Phosphatase 2A complex (GO:0005524); PPP2R1A (HGNC:9000) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal development regulation pathway; Protein Phosphatase 2A complex (GO:0005524) —DECREASES→ Neuronal development regulation pathway; Neuronal development regulation pathway —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal neuronal migration (HP:0001739); Neuronal development regulation pathway —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar hypoplasia (HP:0001272). Loss-of-function mutations in PPP2R1A disrupt the formation or function of the Protein Phosphatase 2A complex, which is critical for regulating neuronal development pathways. This dysregulation leads to phenotypes such as abnormal neuronal migration and cerebellar hypoplasia, observed in both MONDO:0013822 and MONDO:0014605.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PPP2R1A with a consistent loss-of-function effect in both disease cohorts, and demonstration of normal PP2A complex activity in unaffected individuals carrying rare variants. _(variant: The absence of common loss-of-function variants in PPP2R1A in large population databases like gnomAD would support its role in rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of PPP2R1A and PP2A in neuronal development could inform therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring normal neuronal function or mitigating developmental defects in patients with these conditions.
